statement: In recursive Bayesian estimation, the belief distribution over the current state given all observations up to time step k, p(x_k | z_{1:k}), is computed recursively via a prediction step p(x_k | z_{1:k-1}) = \int p(x_k | x_{k-1}) p(x_{k-1} | z_{1:k-1}) d x_{k-1} and an update step p(x_k | z_{1:k}) = \frac{p(z_k | x_k) p(x_k | z_{1:k-1})}{p(z_k | z_{1:k-1})} \propto p(z_k | x_k) p(x_k | z_{1:k-1}).

symbols.meaning: Unobserved true state vector at step k
Observed measurement vector at step k
Sequence of measurements from time step 1 up to time step k
Posterior belief distribution over the state x_k given measurements up to time step k
Predicted belief distribution over state x_k given measurements up to time step k-1
Marginal likelihood normalization factor for the observation z_k

steps.text: Apply the first-order Markov process assumption on states, stating that the state x_k is conditionally independent of all earlier states x_{k-2}, ..., x_0 given x_{k-1}: p(x_k | x_{k-1}, x_{k-2}, \dots, x_0) = p(x_k | x_{k-1}).
Apply the conditional independence assumption on measurements, stating that z_k depends only on x_k: p(z_k | x_k, x_{k-1}, \dots, x_0) = p(z_k | x_k).

Write the joint probability distribution over all states x_0, \dots, x_k and observations z_1, \dots, z_k using the Markov and conditional independence assumptions: p(x_0, \dots, x_k, z_1, \dots, z_k) = p(x_0) \prod_{i=1}^{k} p(z_i | x_i) p(x_i | x_{i-1}).

Compute the predicted belief distribution p(x_k | z_{1:k-1}) by marginalizing out the previous state x_{k-1} from the product of transition probability and previous state belief distribution: p(x_k | z_{1:k-1}) = \int p(x_k | x_{k-1}) p(x_{k-1} | z_{1:k-1}) d x_{k-1}.

Compute the updated belief distribution p(x_k | z_{1:k}) using Bayes' rule to condition on the new measurement z_k: p(x_k | z_{1:k}) = \frac{p(z_k | x_k) p(x_k | z_{1:k-1})}{p(z_k | z_{1:k-1})} \propto p(z_k | x_k) p(x_k | z_{1:k-1}).
Express the normalization denominator by integrating the numerator over all possible states x_k: p(z_k | z_{1:k-1}) = \int p(z_k | x_k) p(x_k | z_{1:k-1}) d x_k.

assumptions.assumption: The state sequence follows a first-order Markov process.
assumptions.breaks_when: The state at step k depends directly on states earlier than step k-1.

assumptions.assumption: Measurements are conditionally independent of all other states and past observations given the current state x_k.
assumptions.breaks_when: Measurement noise is temporally correlated across time steps independently of the underlying state.

failure_modes.mode: Intractable integral in prediction or update steps
failure_modes.signature: Posterior distributions develop increasingly complex non-parametric functional forms over time.
failure_modes.cause: Non-linear transition or observation models, or non-Gaussian noise distributions, prevent closed-form integration.
